newsitem.title: USA: Railroads, unions avert strike over disability pay.
newsitem.headline: Railroads, unions avert strike over disability pay.

text.p: U.S. railroads and their unions averted a nationwide strike threatened for Wednesday with a late agreement to try to reach consensus over a new Railroad Retirement Board disability rule, the sides said.
The threat to strike followed board action to change a rule on evaluating certain disabilities that the unions said would curb benefits to railroad workers.

An official of the National Railway Labor Conference, which represents major carriers, said the carriers were ready to take the unions to court to block a strike that could have tied up freight and passenger service throughout the country.
But the official said the issue was defused when the two sides agreed late Tuesday to try to reach a consensus on how to reform the disability evaluation rule that had been in effect since the 1940s.
A retirement board official said the pending new rule was in proposal form, adding that the board certainly would consider the view of the two sides before issuing any final rule.
The railroad official said no timetable had yet been set for reaching a consensus to submit to the retirement board.
